note: Meets the stated ICP on every criterion. He is not a business owner but he is a senior accounting and finance professional at a hospitality group, which reads as the 'or equivalent' in the stated definition — and the rep's own description of the client base on this very call confirms that is how it is applied in practice: "most of our clients are either business owners or like accountants, doctors." Income is met by conduct: he asked how the payment structure worked, not whether the price was justified, and put $6,000 on a Visa. Good-to-great is unambiguous — 20 lb from target, already lifting four mornings a week and running two half marathons a year, buying the mirror and the mobility rather than a rescue. Nowhere near the deconditioned exclusion. The one criterion worth arguing is neglected_health: he fasts, eats clean, trains consistently and researches protein powder processing, which is not neglect by any ordinary reading. It is counted as a match on the criterion as written — health is the area slipping rather than a crisis, he is 20 lb heavy and has slept badly for two and a half years — but it is the same tension seen with Robert Castillo, where the buyer's health literacy is high and the ICP language assumes it is low. Both closed. The stated ICP may be describing the wrong axis.
